title: Google Docs
subtitle: Order every document's edits in one place, batch the writes, and cap how many people can type at once
motto: Everyone writes at once, so someone must decide the order
keyInsight: The fleet scales by adding machines, but one document must be ordered in one place, so a single busy document is the ceiling that servers cannot lift.

decisions.title: One server orders each document
decisions.description: All edits for a document flow through one collaboration server that transforms and broadcasts them, giving a single total order and no lost edits.
decisions.alternatives: A fully decentralised CRDT spreads ordering but adds per-character metadata and is harder to bound.

decisions.title: Batch the writes, cap the typists
decisions.description: Batching 100 writes cuts the database from 25,000 to 250 nodes for about 5 ms more latency; capping simultaneous typists keeps one document at 80% load.
decisions.alternatives: Writing each edit alone is far too costly, and letting everyone type in a huge document overloads its single ordering server.
